key_insight: UNSM-treated Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings showed sample-dependent hardness, with different treatment settings producing the highest values for detonation-sprayed and HVOF deposits.
engineering_relevance: Treatment selection should balance local hardness with surface integrity rather than assume one UNSM setting suits both deposition routes.
method: Evaluate four UNSM-treated samples per deposition route at 20 or 30 N and 20 or 30 µm vibration amplitude.
Measure instrumental hardness at 300 mN with a 10 s dwell.
evidence_signal: Hardness ranged from 820–970 HV for detonation-sprayed coatings and 546–1165 HV for HVOF coatings, with maxima at 20 N/20 µm and 30 N/30 µm, respectively.
watch_item: Post-scratch SEM observations do not isolate UNSM-induced damage or establish a scratch-resistance ranking.
paper_title: HARDNESS AND POST-SCRATCH SURFACE MORPHOLOGY OF Cr₃C₂–NiCr COATINGS AFTER ULTRASONIC NANOCRYSTAL SURFACE MODIFICATION
